extraction.Name: Nancy Irving
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent to her allotment, covering 320 acres, but that she was told by the Indian Agency that it would be necessary for her to take it
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold it to A. L. Krouse, of Batesland, South Dakota, he taking over this mortgage in favor of Hugo Hoppe
extraction.Buyer: A. L. Krouse, of Batesland, South Dakota, taking over the mortgage in favor of Hugo Hoppe, and paying her the purchase price of $4800.00 for the place, $500.00 in cash, later $400.00 in cash, and again $300.00 in cash; that when making this last payment of $300.00, he told her that this was the final payment, and he has never paid anything since
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: the taxes on this allotment accumulated for six or seven years, and was sold by the County for taxes; then Hugo Hoppe, of Gordon, Nebraska, redeemed it, paying the taxes, and taking a mortgage on the land for his protection; that she was never able to meet these payments
extraction.NOTES: Mentally competent; health is poor, being bothered with heart trouble; has three minor children, two of whom are not very well; sold in March 1926; has never received any help from the County or Government; document No. 479; sworn November 17, 1928 | TASK 5 BULK ALLOTMENT RECOVERY 2026-04-29: Sonnet text-extraction captured the allotment number from the source page header but classified it in NOTES as a 'document number' / 'Document No.' / 'No. NNNN' instead of placing it in the structured Allotment number field. The hypothesis that these document/file references are actually allotment numbers was confirmed via BLM cross-reference (exemplars: Eugene Means 2249, Lucy Patton 6802). This patch corrects 48 records via bulk regex extraction from NOTES with user-supervised review of every HIGH-confidence proposal.

recovery_notes.rationale: Source page header contained 'No. NNNN' which Sonnet captured in NOTES as 'document number' rather than placing in structured Allotment field. Hypothesis confirmed via BLM cross-reference.
